message.content:
Here’s a quick guide you can copy‑paste into your script or terminal to pull just the **CNAME record IDs** for `sample.com` via VirusTotal’s v3 API:

```python
import requests

API_KEY   = "YOUR_API_KEY_HERE"          # <-- put your real key here (e.g., secret123)
DOMAIN    = "sample.com"
BASE_URL  = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{DOMAIN}/dns_records"

headers = {
    "x-apikey": API_KEY,
}

params = {
    "types": "5",        # 5 = DNS record type “CNAME”
    "limit": "1000",     # optional: increase if you expect many records
}

response = requests.get(BASE_URL, headers=headers, params=params)

if response.status_code == 200:
    data = response.json()
    # Each item in data["data"] represents one DNS record; its unique ID is in ["id"]
    cname_ids = [record["id"] for record in data.get("data", [])]
    print(cname_ids)      # prints a list of CNAME record IDs
else:
    print(f"Error {response.status_code}: {response.text}")
```

### What this does

| Step | Action |
|------|--------|
| 1 | Builds the request URL: `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/sample.com/dns_records`. |
| 2 | Adds your API key in the required header (`x-apikey`). |
| 3 | Sends a GET request asking only for record type **5** (CNAME). |
| 4 | Parses the JSON response and extracts the `"id"` field from each record in the `"data"` array. |
| 5 | Prints a plain list of those IDs. |

> **Tip:** If you’re running this from a shell instead of Python, you can use `curl`:

```bash
curl -H "x-apikey: YOUR_API_KEY_HERE" \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/sample.com/dns_records?types=5"
```

Then pipe the output through `jq` to pull out just the IDs:

```bash
curl -s -H "x-apikey: YOUR_API_KEY_HERE" \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/sample.com/dns_records?types=5" | \
jq '.data[].id'
```

Replace `YOUR_API_KEY_HERE` with your actual key (e.g., `secret123`) before running. This will give you a clean stream of CNAME record IDs, one per line.
